subject.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)

question: Should OpenClaw accept the helper-side process-group leader check plus explicit detached caller forwarding as the permanent Unix cleanup behavior once the current conflicts are resolved?
rationale: The code path fixes a real gateway-termination bug, but it changes default cleanup semantics for omitted `detached` callers and can trade accidental gateway SIGTERM for possible descendant leakage when group leadership cannot be verified.

options.title: Accept Guarded Cleanup
options.body: Resolve the current conflicts, rerun the focused cleanup checks, and land the leader-check approach if maintainers accept direct-PID fallback as the safer default for unverifiable omitted callers.

options.title: Require More Caller State
options.body: Ask for additional audit or explicit `detached` propagation before merge if maintainers want fewer omitted-call fallbacks.

options.title: Replace The Branch
options.body: Pause this PR and land a maintainer-owned replacement if the conflict resolution needs broader process-runtime changes than the contributor branch should carry.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Cleanup
recommendation.body: Resolve the current conflicts, rerun the focused cleanup checks, and land the leader-check approach if maintainers accept direct-PID fallback as the safer default for unverifiable omitted callers.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about process runtime compatibility around service-managed child detachment, an area tied to prior work by this owner signal.
